md-aaliyah-162cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: One Chapter Longer
md-aaliyah-162cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: By the time you arrive, Aaliyah is leaning back in a dark green chair, surrounded by a lush curtain of leaves that seem to isolate the room from the outside world. Her dark braids frame her face as she looks up, one finger keeping her place in a book. Flowers sit near the green chair, their shapes echoed by her earrings above the lime mesh of her top. Beyond the leaves, a clock announces that you are both late. You suggest leaving now. Aaliyah suggests one more chapter, then slides the book across and asks you to read. Suddenly you are negotiating against yourself.

md-amanda-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: The Carefully Kept Note
md-amanda-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: On a purple sofa, Amanda divides her attention between a blue bottle and a single red rose. She studies the flower with a distant expression, the black fabric of her outfit blending into the shadows of the room. A decorative cord rests loosely in her fingers while you try to explain a mysterious note left at the door. When she notices you, her gaze is steady and intrigued, as if you have interrupted a very important mystery. Amanda asks whether you checked the other side. You turn the paper over and find the missing address. She has been waiting a remarkably long time for you to think of that.

md-ann-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: One Sentence Shorter
md-ann-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: Against a clay-warm wall, Ann leans back while the sunlight traces a sharp line across her short ash-brown hair. You have just begun a long story when she tilts her head, a small smile suggesting she has already guessed your punchline. In her black cutout top, she glances at the clock on the wall, then back at you with exaggerated patience. When you ask if she is bored, she requests the short version. You deliver it in one sentence. Ann laughs, declares it excellent, and wonders why you kept that version to yourself.

md-bella-167cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: No Spoilers Tonight
md-bella-167cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: In a dim library, Bella has claimed the single beam of sunlight for herself. She wears a dark collared dress and focuses on the open book in her hands, her gaze steady and absorbed. For a moment, she doesn't notice your arrival, her attention on the page until she suddenly looks over the rim of her glasses. A dry smile touches her lips as she marks her place, closing the volume with a slow, deliberate motion. She asks whether you have read the ending. You admit you have not. Bella opens the book again and offers the chair beside her. Apparently this conversation has a reading requirement, but absolutely no spoilers.

md-bellamy-162cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: A Different Record
md-bellamy-162cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: “Train with me or advise from over there?” Bellamy asks, resting beside the black exercise chair in an otherwise empty gym. Strands of brown hair with lighter highlights fall across her shoulder as she considers the weights on the floor. Still in her green printed top, she asks whether you have come to train or merely offer advice. As you approach, she signals for you to join her, though her focus remains fixed on the next set. You propose calling it a night. Bellamy agrees, on the condition that you carry the weights back first. Your best performance of the evening turns out to be cleanup.

md-brianna-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: The First Round
md-brianna-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: Boxing gloves on and grinning, Brianna challenges you to a quick training session. As she raises one glove to invite you into the center of the ring, a sharp, knowing smile tugs at her lips. She stands poised and ready, the bold red of her athletic gear mirroring a spirit that refuses to take a step back. You explain that you have studied the technique extensively. Brianna asks whether any of that studying involved leaving the sofa. The first round becomes a lesson in footwork, and your impressive theory has to find somewhere useful to stand.

md-coco-164cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: A Table Outside
md-coco-164cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: Low lights in a dim jazz club catch the white fabric of Coco's collared outfit as she saves you a seat. Her brown hair falls in light-tipped waves over her shoulders, shimmering whenever she leans in to hear you speak. With a slight tilt of her head, her dangling earrings sway, reflecting the hushed energy of the surrounding cocktail lounge. She asks about your day, her chain necklaces resting against her chest, as she considers whether to order a second round. Before you can answer, the band launches into another solo. Coco points toward the terrace and mouths a practical suggestion: take the conversation somewhere it can actually be heard. You have never agreed to a change of venue so quickly.

md-eileen-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: The Wrong Label
md-eileen-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: There is Eileen, tucked away in the living room and carefully inspecting a striped decoration while the party buzzes in the next room. Her red outfit stands out against the ornaments of the tree, bright among the ribbons and ornaments. When you approach, she deftly hides a wrapped gift behind her back, a playful glimmer in her eyes suggesting you are not supposed to see it yet. She asks you to guess whose name is on the label. You try everyone at the party before she turns it around: the gift is for the host, and you are supposed to help find the missing tag. Mystery solved, useful work begins.

md-ellema-167cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: The Record Dispute
md-ellema-167cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: Pink light washes over a dim lounge, and an old record plays somewhere behind the sofa. Ellema is there, reclining on a light-colored sofa with her sunglasses pushed back into her hair. She doesn't move when you arrive, merely tilting her head to let the record sleeve slide from her lap. With a fur-textured collar hugging her neck, she traces the edge of the album cover and asks if you recognize the artist. You recognize the cover and confidently name the wrong artist. Ellema turns the sleeve around so you can read it for yourself. She is willing to let you choose the next record, provided you promise to check the label first.

md-fiona-162cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: The Missing Last Verse
md-fiona-162cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: Warm golden light from a September afternoon settles on Fiona as she pauses among the hay bales, her brown layered hair catching the glow while she tunes her guitar. Her hoop earrings shimmer while she hums a low, lingering melody, trying the same unfinished verse for the third time. In her white printed top and denim shorts, she looks as though she has been waiting for someone to wander off the beaten path. When she notices you, Fiona stops playing and asks for a rhyme. Your first suggestion earns a laugh; the second earns a place in the chorus. She says the song is finally finished, provided nobody ever hears your first suggestion.

md-gianna-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: The Unplayed Request
md-gianna-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: Halfway through the evening, Gianna leans back on the sofa, her fingers resting against the strings of an electric guitar. Still in her black two-piece outfit, she asks which song you have been trying to remember all evening. You ask if she remembers the chords to that rare track you mentioned, and she tilts her head, considering your increasingly unreliable description. Before you can answer, she switches off the amplifier with a wink, choosing a quieter route for the evening. She explains that she knows the song, but your attempt to hum it deserves a discussion of its own. The concert can wait until you both stop laughing.

md-grace-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: An Early Exit
md-grace-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: Long before the party winds down, Grace steals away from the crowded room and slips into the dim corridor where the noise becomes a distant murmur. In her lavender ruched dress, she lingers by a heavy velvet curtain, watching the door while another speech begins beyond the curtain. Grace raises one arm, tucking a stray lock of hair behind her ear as she studies the room for anyone who might follow. She asks whether the fifth toast is compulsory. You say you stopped counting at three. That settles it: there is a late supper to find, and neither of you intends to give a speech over it.

md-hazel-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: Before the Wax Sets
md-hazel-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: Nobody else notices Hazel in the dim glow of a few stray candles, her red braids draped over her shoulders as she tends to the flickering light. She doesn't look up when you enter, focused instead on the wax dripping slow and steady. Wearing a dark green top that blends into the shadows, she seems completely unaware of the time or the world outside the heavy drapes. As you draw closer, Hazel offers a faint, enigmatic smile and suggests you stay a while. She has been attempting to rescue a candle that leans persistently to one side. You offer an elaborate solution; Hazel turns the holder around and solves it at once. There is still time to pretend you suggested that.

md-heather-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: The Familiar Chorus
md-heather-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: Only the electric guitar resting against the sofa hints at the last song as Heather takes a breather in the dim living room. She lets her headphones hang around her neck, considering the next song while you try to name the one that just ended. With a nod toward the instrument and her silver top catching a stray beam of light, she suggests a change in the setlist to something less predictable. You recognize the opening notes of the next track and announce your victory too soon. Heather stops it before the chorus and asks for the title. For once, the person holding the headphones also holds the answer.

md-jeane-167cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: A Better Ending
md-jeane-167cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: One corner of a textured blanket is already Jeane's, and she is waiting for you to finish the last page of your book. In her black outfit, she waits with the patience of someone who suspects the ending will disappoint you. She crosses her legs and asks whether the mysterious letter has finally been opened. You reach the last line and close the book. Jeane takes one look at your face and offers to invent a better ending. Her version is considerably shorter, and the letter arrives on time. You decide the author should have consulted her first.

md-jennifer-166cm-silicone-companion-dol.heading: A Different Show
md-jennifer-166cm-silicone-companion-dol.paragraph: Under the marquee lights, Jennifer's gold outfit shimmers as she stands by the theater doors. She adjusts the light-colored hat perched atop her head, nodding toward a passing car with a conspiratorial smile. While others study the playbill, she wants you to venture away from the crowd to find a spot where the city noise softens. With a simple shrug of her jacket, she begins to lead the way, her movements graceful and light. She has spotted a tiny restaurant across the street, with one empty table by the window. You ask about missing the first act. Jennifer says you have already read the reviews; dinner deserves a fair hearing too.

md-joanna-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: A Well-Lit Detour
md-joanna-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: Just as the stars appear, you meet Joanna on the ancient stone path behind the gardens. She waits in the shadows of towering pines, her patterned wrap draped loosely about her shoulders. The lantern in her hand casts a warm, amber glow that reveals the curve of her arm raised in a silent summons. She explains that the main gate has been locked, although the evening itself is far from over. With a hint of a smile, she guides you away from the noise of the party. You ask whether this shortcut is shorter. Joanna admits it is not, but there is a bakery at the other end that stays open late. The lantern has suddenly become a very persuasive argument.

md-judy-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: The Easy Wish
md-judy-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: Every head turns toward the doorway of the darkened ballroom as Judy appears, her white embellished dress catching the stray beams of moonlight. She asks if you have seen the garden terrace and leads you quietly toward the heavy velvet curtains. As you step outside, she studies the constellations with a focused, searching expression. Her dark accessory held between her fingers glints as she tilts her head, noting that the stars are aligned for an impossible request. Her impossible request turns out to be ten uninterrupted minutes away from small talk. You promise not to mention the weather, the music, or the guest list. Judy says you are already doing rather well.

md-kamari-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: The Unfinished Story
md-kamari-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: Seconds before you close the door for the night, Kamari strides into the room. Her printed white outfit glows against the dimming light, and she offers a small, knowing smile that suggests she has a question requiring your full attention. Seated on the edge of a nearby chair with her legs crossed, she waits for you to speak first, her hands resting patiently. She reminds you that you left a story unfinished at dinner, precisely at the interesting part. You claim it was not much of a story. Kamari settles more comfortably into the chair and asks you to let her be the judge. Closing time has acquired a small extension.

md-leona-161cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: The Unscheduled Meeting
md-leona-161cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: Leona has claimed the corner booth of a nearly empty lounge, her dark hair tucked neatly beneath a black cap. She watches the entrance with a steady gaze, her expression unreadable as she draws her white wrap tighter against the sudden chill. When you finally slide into the brown upholstered chair opposite her, she offers no greeting. Instead, she leans forward, her red-and-black outfit catching the dim light as she gestures for you to listen closely. Her proposition is simple: abandon the crowded reception and find somewhere that serves dinner after midnight. You came prepared for intrigue. Leona came prepared with a reservation.

md-luna-162cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: The Hat Has Spoken
md-luna-162cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: You find Luna reclining against the yellow cushions of the sofa, the brim of her straw hat casting a soft shadow over her dark hair. While the rest of the house is warm and still, she rests beside you, the white beads of her necklace catching the filtered sunlight. She suggests a walk just as you settle into the sofa, turning your attention away from the books scattered nearby. When you ask where she wants to go, Luna merely smiles and taps the side of her hat. You point out that neither of you has a map. Luna says that is rather the point. The books will still be there when you return; this particular afternoon will not.

md-mary-168cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: A Reason to Linger
md-mary-168cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: Down the hall, Mary has tucked herself away in a candlelit alcove, where the scent of a single rose lingers in the air. While the rest of the room hums with conversation, she remains still, her presence marked by a companionable silence beneath a delicate black veil. A glimpse of purple fabric catches the low light as she shifts, her steady gaze meeting yours with an invitation to forget the crowd. She asks you to count how many conversations you can hear without joining any of them. You lose track at four. Mary declares the experiment a success: neither of you has had to discuss the weather for several excellent minutes.

md-nia-162cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: The Spare Pair
md-nia-162cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: At the far end of a glass-walled sunroom, where the air smells of damp earth and distant rain, Nia is deep in her own world. Her long black hair spills over a leopard-pattern robe as she rearranges the monstera leaves, a blue flower tucked behind her ear. When she notices you, she doesn't stop her work; she simply asks if you brought the pruning shears. Her white bead necklace shifts as she points toward a stubborn branch just beyond reach. You admit you thought this was a social call. Nia points to a spare pair of gardening gloves and agrees that it is. Apparently good company comes with a small amount of pruning.

md-rose-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: A Useful Interruption
md-rose-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: Before the afternoon fades, Rose settles into the amber glow of the sunroom, her small bouquet resting casually on the table between you. She wears a gold patterned outfit that echoes the warm light, while her sunglasses remain perched atop her head. A gentle tilt of her chin and a hand resting thoughtfully beside her face suggest she is listening to your story with a secret of her own. You work through the details of an unnecessarily complicated afternoon, stopping only when she lifts a hand. Rose asks which part you would like to repeat tomorrow. You answer none of it. She pushes the bouquet aside to make room for a clean sheet of paper. That seems a sensible place to start.

md-sally-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: One Stop Earlier
md-sally-166cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: Late in the day, Sally has disappeared into the pages of her magazine, oblivious to the bustle of the crowded station. A pair of headphones rests around her neck while her white sunglasses shield her from the prying eyes of the morning commute. She seems perfectly content in her own world until you discover her hidden bookstore guide tucked between glossy pages. With a sudden, knowing smile, she offers you a seat beside her and begins to point out the best used-book shops in the city. Your train arrives while she is circling one address. Sally asks whether you really need to be anywhere yet. You look from the timetable to the magazine and decide that one missed train is an acceptable price for a better afternoon.

md-vicky-163cm-silicone-companion-doll.heading: The Better Destination
md-vicky-163cm-silicone-companion-doll.paragraph: The cab has barely pulled over in the city when Vicky leans across to rewrite your destination on the slip. Her long blonde hair catches the glare of the sun and she pushes her white sunglasses up to study the street signs. As the car eases toward the sound of the surf, she tells you that the most treasured spots don't appear on any tourist brochure. Clad in a yellow floral swimsuit, she studies the passing scenery with an air of genuine curiosity. You mention that the hotel has a perfectly good pool. Vicky points toward the open coast and asks whether the pool has a horizon. You stop defending the hotel.
